# Planar stationary groups: exact weighted accounting and an overlap obstruction

This note concerns q=d=2. It uses the already proved ordinary planar
theorem in `candidate c22519c29667168e`: if proper
sections of a convex planar body have the same midpoint y and
probabilities theta_i satisfy `sum theta_i S_i u_i=0`, where u_i are
unit cap normals and S_i are chord lengths, then

    sum_i theta_i |K intersect H_i| >= (4/9)|K|.       (1)

No such local stationarity is asserted for arbitrary original-cap
groups selected by Helly and Doignon. The result below identifies a
precise sufficient condition and the exact accounting error when
one part of that condition fails.

## 1. A sharp warning about unweighted overlap charges

Let T=conv{(0,0),(1,0),(0,1)}, of area 1/2, and let y=(3/10,3/10).
Take the three closed halfplanes

    H_0={x+y_coord<=3/5},
    H_1={3x−y_coord>=3/5},
    H_2={3y_coord−x>=3/5}.

Here y_coord denotes the second coordinate, to distinguish it from
the common contact point. All boundaries pass through y. Their
affine margins satisfy `2L_0+L_1+L_2=0`, so the halfplanes cover
the entire plane and form a minimal positive normal circuit.

The chords have endpoints

    H_0: (3/5,0), (0,3/5),
    H_1: (1/5,0), (2/5,3/5),
    H_2: (0,1/5), (3/5,2/5).

Every chord midpoint is exactly y. The cap fractions are

    (|T intersect H_0|,|T intersect H_1|,|T intersect H_2|)/|T|
       =(9/25,12/25,12/25).

All three are strictly below 1/2. Their pair-intersection fractions
are respectively

    |H_0 intersect H_1 intersect T|/|T|=3/25,
    |H_0 intersect H_2 intersect T|/|T|=3/25,
    |H_1 intersect H_2 intersect T|/|T|=2/25.

These intersections are triangles; their vertices follow by
intersecting the displayed lines with the three edges of T. The
triple intersection is the single point y. Therefore the actual
multiplicity overlap is

    sum_i |T intersect H_i|−|T|=(8/25)|T|<|T|/3.      (2)

Thus even a stationary common contact and three cap fractions below
1/2 do NOT justify the unweighted overlap charge |K|/3 that would
turn the ordinary three-cap sum estimate into 4/9. This example
already uses actual intersections in one convex body, so neither
convex compatibility nor retaining intersection volumes repairs
that particular charge.

The correct section-weighted calculation remains valid. The vectors
S_i u_i are

    (−3/5,−3/5), (3/5,−1/5), (−1/5,3/5).

They balance with probabilities `(1/4,3/8,3/8)`. The corresponding
weighted cap fraction is exactly 9/20, exceeding 4/9 by 1/180.
The strict deficit in the unweighted overlap bound is 1/75 of |T|.

## 2. The weighted incidence identity retains which regions overlap

For any three proper concurrent halfplanes with a minimal positive
normal circuit, their union is the plane and their triple
intersection has area zero. Within a planar convex body write E_i
for the region captured only by cap i, and D_i for the region
captured by the other two caps but not i. Ignore their null line
boundaries, and write e_i=|E_i|, d_i=|D_i|.

For every probability vector theta there is the exact identity

    sum_i theta_i |K intersect H_i|
      =sum_i theta_i e_i+sum_i(1−theta_i)d_i.          (3)

Thus (1), when its midpoint hypotheses hold, is a genuinely weighted
incidence inequality. The unweighted overlap `sum_i d_i` forgets
which pair overlaps, and is insufficient to replace (3) by the
uniform coefficients required in (2).

## 3. One common section profile gives one shared cap budget

Let a full mixed-volume set with d=2 have positive fibers K_z and
total mass M. Suppose k groups of actual original caps are given,
and partition the positive base indices into ownership sets P_j,
so the jth group covers every fiber it owns. Put

    S_j=union_(z∈P_j) ({z} times K_z), W_j=mu(S_j).

For each three-cap group assume its continuous unit normals u_ji
form a minimal positive circuit; fix positive coefficients rho_ji
with `sum_i rho_ji u_ji=0`. On every owned fiber require that all
three sections are proper and have one common midpoint. Finally,
suppose their chord lengths have a common profile:

    S_ji(z)=a_z s_ji,   a_z>0, s_ji>0.               (4)

Then define the single probability vector for this group by

    theta_ji=(rho_ji/s_ji)/sum_l(rho_jl/s_jl).

Equation (4) makes `sum_i theta_ji S_ji(z)u_ji=0` on
EVERY owned fiber. Summing (1) and retaining outside-fiber cap mass
gives

    sum_i theta_ji mu(H_ji) >= (4/9)W_j.

If all original caps have mass at most B, the left side is at most
B, independently of the number of caps in the group. Therefore

    k B >= (4/9)M.                                   (5)

In particular k≤2^n gives the OC cap-cover budget for this stated
class. A one-cap group owning wholly captured fibers obeys the
stronger B≥W_j. A two-cap group covering its owned fibers obeys
B≥W_j/2 by its ordinary union bound, also sufficient for (5).
These cases need no midpoint or section-profile assumption.

This is a sufficient theorem about covers with the indicated local
geometry, not a claim that an arbitrary selected cover has it.

## 4. Exact dispersion error and actual cross-capture credit

Keep the proper common-midpoint assumption for every three-cap
group on each owned fiber, but drop (4). Its uniquely determined
section-balancing probabilities are

    theta_ji(z)=(rho_ji/S_ji(z))/sum_l(rho_jl/S_jl(z)).

Write p_ji(z)=|K_z intersect H_ji|/w_z and
R_j(z)=max_i p_ji(z)−min_i p_ji(z). For any single chosen group
probability vector theta_j define

    E_j(theta_j)=sum_(z∈P_j) w_z R_j(z)
                         * (1/2)sum_i|theta_ji−theta_ji(z)|,
    X_j(theta_j)=sum_i theta_ji mu(H_ji intersect (S\S_j)).

The first is the explicit section-profile dispersion cost; the
second is actual weighted cap mass on fibers owned by other groups.
For probability vectors theta,theta' and real numbers p_i with
range R,

    sum_i(theta_i−theta'_i)p_i >= −R*TV(theta,theta').

Indeed subtract min p from all coordinates; the negative part of
theta−theta' has total mass TV, and each remaining p lies in [0,R].
Applying this to (1) on each owned fiber proves

    B >= (4/9)W_j − E_j(theta_j)+X_j(theta_j).         (6)

Summing preserves ONE budget B per group:

For any one- or two-cap groups, use their stronger coarse bounds
from Section 3 and set E_j=X_j=0 in this summation.

    kB >= (4/9)M + sum_j[X_j(theta_j)−E_j(theta_j)].   (7)

Consequently nonnegative total credit in (7) is a rigorous
sufficient condition for the desired 4/9 allocation. Common
profiles have E_j=0, recovering (5). For each fixed actual cover,
maximizing X_j−E_j over theta_j is an attained finite linear
program after introducing the usual absolute-value slack variables.
There is no selection limit or hidden change in the source.

No sign for the total credit is asserted in general. Nor do arbitrary
groups have the section-midpoint property required to invoke (1).
The formula isolates these two missing geometric conditions rather
than assuming them from continuous normal balance or fiberwise
covering. It is distinct from simply reapplying the scalar
convex-majorant inequalities: actual cap incidence on other owned
fibers remains in X_j, and the local weights are fixed by actual
section lengths.

All bodies and sections in this note are ordinary full planar
fibers. An intrinsic extension with changing two-dimensional
direction spaces is not asserted. The finite original-cap group
selection theorem supplies ownership but by itself supplies neither
the common-midpoint assumption nor proportional section profiles.
